title: ESPD Instance Data — Part III (Exclusion grounds)
description: EXPERIMENTAL canonical instance-data model for Part III of the ESPD standard form: exclusion grounds. Scoped for now to a single criterion, C01 (exg-crim-part, 'Participation in a criminal organisation'), used as a probe for the more complex criterion structures. Models instance data only — deliberately independent of the form definition, UI, and XML serialization. Code-list values are bare codes.

partIII.description: Information concerning exclusion grounds and (later) selection criteria.

exclusionGrounds.description: Exclusion-ground criteria keyed by the stable criterion code (the ESPD-EDM `code`, e.g. 'exg-crim-part'). Keying by semantic code rather than by form tag (C01) keeps the instance data stable if the form re-numbers criteria. Each criterion holds BOTH request (buyer) and response (economic operator) data via `requirement`/`response` sub-objects (see docs/model-xml-mapping.md). Exclusion grounds carry NO buyer data — the buyer only selects that the ground applies, which is fixed criterion metadata (from e-Certis), not instance data — so `requirement` is absent and `response` holds the economic operator's answer. Only criteria actually present in the exchange need appear.

convictionCriterion.description: An exclusion criterion of the 'conviction' shape (C01–C06 in Section A share this structure). Split into `requirement` (buyer/request side) and `response` (economic-operator side), mirroring the ESPD document boundary. Exclusion grounds carry NO buyer data, so `requirement` is absent here; it exists in the model only for symmetry with selection criteria (which do carry buyer thresholds). `response` holds the economic operator's answer.

requirement.$comment: Buyer/request side. Not applicable to exclusion grounds (the buyer only selects that the ground applies — fixed criterion metadata, not instance data). Present in the shape only for symmetry with selection criteria; expected to be absent for C01–C06.

convictionResponse.description: The economic operator's answer to a conviction-shaped exclusion ground. `answer` is the yes/no reply (C01/QG1/Q1). When true, one or more `convictions` describe each relevant conviction (C01/QG1/QSG1, cardinality 0..n). `electronicEvidence` (C01/QG2) states whether the information is available electronically and, if so, references the evidence.

answer.description: Whether the exclusion ground applies to the economic operator (C01/QG1/Q1, INDICATOR). Maps to a criterion response indicator in UBL.

convictions.description: Details of each relevant conviction (C01/QG1/QSG1, cardinality 0..n). Only meaningful when `answer` is true; each entry maps to a repeated response set in UBL.

allOf.$comment: Structural conditionality mirroring the form's ONTRUE code: conviction detail is only relevant when the ground is answered 'yes'. Encoded as a soft constraint — when answer is false, no convictions should be supplied.

conviction.description: A single conviction relevant to the exclusion ground (C01/QG1/QSG1).

dateOfConviction.description: Date of the conviction (C01/QG1/QSG1/Q1, DATE). ISO 8601 date.

period.description: Length of the period of exclusion (C01/QG1/QSG1/Q4, PERIOD). The form asks a single free-text question, but the underlying datatype is a period; modeled as an object so it can carry a human description now and structured start/end dates later without a breaking change. Maps to UBL cac:Period.

description.description: Free-text description of the exclusion period as entered on the form (maps to cbc:Description).

startDate.description: Optional start of the exclusion period (maps to cbc:StartDate).

endDate.description: Optional end of the exclusion period (maps to cbc:EndDate).

selfCleaning.description: Self-cleaning measures taken to demonstrate reliability despite the conviction (C01/QG1/QSG1/QSG1). `taken` is the indicator answer; `description` is only relevant when `taken` is true (the form nests it under ONTRUE).

taken.description: Whether measures have been taken to demonstrate reliability (C01/QG1/QSG1/QSG1/Q1, INDICATOR).

description.description: Description of the self-cleaning measures (C01/QG1/QSG1/QSG1/QSG1/Q1, DESCRIPTION). Expected only when `taken` is true.

allOf.$comment: Mirrors the form's ONTRUE nesting: a description is only relevant when measures were taken.

electronicEvidence.description: The 'is this information available electronically?' block (C01/QG2). This same pattern recurs across every exclusion ground and selection criterion, so it is factored into a shared definition. `availableElectronically` is the indicator; when true, `evidence` lists one or more evidence references (C01/QG2/QSG1/Q1, EVIDENCE_IDENTIFIER, cardinality 1..n).

availableElectronically.description: Whether the supporting information/documentation is available electronically (C01/QG2/Q1, INDICATOR).

evidence.description: References to the electronically-available evidence (C01/QG2/QSG1/Q1, EVIDENCE_IDENTIFIER). Expected (1..n) only when `availableElectronically` is true.

allOf.$comment: Mirrors ONTRUE: evidence is only relevant when the information is available electronically, and at least one evidence reference is then expected.

evidenceReference.description: A reference to a piece of evidence available electronically. Aligns with UBL cac:Evidence. NOTE the two distinct identities: `id` is the evidence entity's OWN identity (owned by the producer of this instance data), which the XML mapping uses as cac:Evidence/cbc:ID and as the cac:EvidenceSupplied/cbc:ID link target; `identifier` is the identity of the underlying document/record (e.g. a certificate number), a separate cac:DocumentReference/cbc:ID.

id.description: The evidence entity's own identity, supplied by the producer. Used to cross-link the answer to this evidence in the UBL XML (cac:EvidenceSupplied/cbc:ID -> cac:Evidence/cbc:ID). Must be unique within the document.

url.description: URL where the evidence can be accessed.

identifier.description: Optional identifier of the underlying document/record (e.g. a certificate number). Distinct from `id`.

description.description: Optional human description of the evidence.
